questions.text: At village clinics in Xiantao, China, how did assignment to a prescribing package using both C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A, compared with usual care, affect antibiotic prescribing at the initial consultation for acute respiratory infection?

scope.population: Initial acute respiratory infection consultations in patients of all ages at 40 village clinics in Xiantao, Hubei, China
scope.factor: Clinic assignment to combined C-reactive protein and serum amyloid A point-of-care testing with a prescribing algorithm, clinician training, desk reminders, monthly prescribing feedback, patient education and a test copayment paid to the clinician
scope.comparator: Clinic assignment to usual care without the combined test, additional clinician training or patient education materials
scope.outcome: Any antibiotic prescription from the village clinician at the index consultation

sources.citation: Xu M, Wang J, Zhang Z, Ge E, Zhu Y, Li J, Gong Y, Lu Z, Wei X, Yin X. Lancet Reg Health West Pac. 2026, volume 71, article 101888. DOI 10.1016/j.lanwpc.2026.101888.
